mainTopic: Which slaves make wine into יין נסך, and a case of wine stirred by a גוי in מחוזא.
overview: The amud finishes quoting a ברייתא about slaves who were circumcised but not yet immersed. Their spittle and the things they tread on are impure (some say pure). The adults among them make wine into יין נסך, and the minors do not. The גמרא challenges an earlier view from this ברייתא, because it seems to say that once slaves are circumcised and immersed they no longer forbid wine. It answers that this leniency is about בני שפחות, who were raised in a Jewish home. A back-and-forth over the word "וכן" ends with the lesson that slaves follow the same adult/minor rule as בני שפחות. This rejects רב, who held that even a one-day-old baby makes wine into יין נסך. The גמרא then tells of a גוי in מחוזא who stirred wine in a Jew's store, and the owner angrily poured it into a barrel. רבא allowed the barrel to be sold to גוים, while רב הונא בר חיננא and רב הונא בר רב נחמן forbade it, and both courts announced their rulings with שופר blasts.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: spittle, treading, and wine of slaves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its rulings. The spittle and treading of these slaves are impure (some say pure). The adults among them make wine into יין נסך, but the minors do not. Adults are those who understand עבודה זרה and its objects.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their spittle and the things they tread on, even in the marketplace, are impure, and some say they are pure. As for their wine: the adults make it into libation wine, but the minors do not. Who counts as an adult and who counts as a minor? Adults are those who know what idol worship and its objects are all about. Minors are those who do not know this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a ברייתא about slaves who were circumcised but not yet immersed. This ברייתא will be the basis for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate rulings here. The first is about טומאה, meaning spittle and treading, and on this there is a dispute between impure and pure. The second is about wine. Here the deciding factor is not physical age but whether the slave understands עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Their spittle and the objects they tread on (questions of טומאה).
Wine forbidden because it may have been used for idol worship.
Here: those who understand idol worship versus those who do not.
The nature of idol worship and the objects used to serve it.

steps.confusionAlert: Here גדולים and קטנים do not mean grown-ups and children by age. They mean those who understand עבודה זרה and those who do not.

phrases.english: in the marketplace, is impure,
phrases.notes: This is talking about their spittle and the things they tread on, which the ברייתא mentioned just before this.

phrases.english: and some say: pure.
Their wine —
adults make it libation wine,
minors do not make it libation wine.

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ הֵן גְּדוֹלִים וְאֵלּוּ הֵן קְטַנִּים?
phrases.english: Who are adults and who are minors?
Adults — those who know the nature of
idol worship and its objects,
minors — those who do not know the nature of
idol worship and its objects.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote of a ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaves who were circumcised but not immersed: their spittle and treading are impure (or pure, according to the other version). The adults who understand עבודה זרה make wine into יין נסך, and the minors do not.

steps.title: The ברייתא implies circumcised and immersed slaves do not forbid wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא only forbids wine when the slaves were circumcised but not immersed. That suggests that once they are immersed, their wine is fine, which challenges the earlier view.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches: if they were circumcised but did not immerse, yes, they forbid wine. But if they were circumcised and immersed, no, they do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely to attack the earlier view. That view held that such slaves can still forbid wine even after immersion, until they forget עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא specifically says "circumcised but not immersed." The גמרא infers that circumcised and immersed slaves do not forbid wine at all, even if they have not yet forgotten idol worship. This contradicts the earlier position.

keyTerms.meaning: "In any event, it teaches," used to pull out the relevant point from a source.
They were circumcised but did not immerse.
Yes / no, used to contrast two cases.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
circumcised and not immersed — yes,
phrases.notes: Meaning: yes, these slaves forbid the wine they touch.

phrases.english: circumcised and immersed — no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted to challenge the earlier view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier view that circumcised and immersed slaves still forbid wine until they forget עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא limits the ruling to slaves who were not immersed. That implies immersed slaves do not forbid wine at all.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about sons of maidservants
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about בני שפחות. These are slaves born to maidservants and raised in a Jewish home, who never served idols.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain the ברייתא as talking about sons of maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It narrows which slaves the ברייתא's implied leniency is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בני שפחות grew up in a Jewish home and never practiced עבודה זרה, so they have nothing to forget. For them, circumcision and immersion are enough. Slaves bought from גוים can still forbid wine until they forget idol worship.

keyTerms.meaning: "Explain it as," narrowing what a source is talking about.
Sons of maidservants, born and raised in a Jewish household.

phrases.english: Explain it as referring to sons of maidservants.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the source is about a specific type of slave.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's leniency for immersed slaves applies to all slaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency applies only to בני שפחות, who never served idols.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says "and likewise"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ברייתא links slaves bought from גוים and sons of maidservants with the word "וכן". That suggests the same ruling applies to both groups.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 3. The wording of the ברייתא seems to treat both groups the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions bought slaves and then says "and likewise sons of maidservants." If both are equal, the ruling cannot apply only to בני שפחות.

keyTerms.meaning: "But it teaches 'and likewise'!", an objection based on a linking word.

phrases.english: But it teaches "and likewise"!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא said bought slaves "and likewise" sons of maidservants, putting the two groups together.

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא is only about בני שפחות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "וכן" makes the two groups equal, so the ruling cannot be limited to one of them.

steps.title: "And likewise" is only about spittle and treading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the "וכן" links the two groups only for the rulings about spittle and treading, not for wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The "and likewise" is about their spittle and the things they tread on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It limits what "וכן" refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two groups are equal only on the question of טומאה, meaning spittle and treading. On wine they can still differ, so the answer from step 3 holds.

phrases.english: It is about their spittle and their treading.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the linking word.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "וכן" makes the two groups equal for every ruling, including wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: "וכן" makes them equal only for spittle and treading.

steps.title: That answer only works for the opinion that says impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this answer works only for the opinion that spittle and treading are impure. For the opinion that they are pure, the "וכן" would be pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says impure. But according to the one who says pure, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 5, using the dispute (impure or pure) from the ברייתא. The next step answers this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If spittle and treading are pure, it is obvious that this applies to בני שפחות too, so there would be no need to say "וכן" about them. In that case the "וכן" must be about wine, and the challenge from step 4 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: "This works well according to the one who says", which sets up a challenge from the other opinion.
"What can be said?" The answer does not fit this opinion.

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says impure,
but for the one who says pure,
what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טָמֵא, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר טָהוֹר, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that "וכן" refers only to spittle and treading.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the opinion that they are pure, there is nothing new to say about בני שפחות, so the "וכן" must be about wine.

steps.title: The link teaches that only adults make wine forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that "וכן" compares slaves to בני שפחות in one way: adults make wine into יין נסך, and minors do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the ברייתא is teaching us: slaves are like sons of maidservants. With sons of maidservants, only adults turn wine into יין נסך, and little children do not. The same is true of slaves: adults turn wine into יין נסך, and little children do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6 by giving the word "וכן" a different job. It is not about immersion at all. It teaches that the adult/minor rule is the same for both groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, the "וכן" seemed pointless for the opinion that spittle and treading are pure. Now the גמרא gives it a real purpose for everyone. Just as with בני שפחות, only an adult slave makes wine forbidden by touching it, and a minor slave does not.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Similar to, compared to
Sons of maidservants (slaves born and raised in a Jewish home)
Wine poured to an idol, or wine forbidden because a גוי touched it
Adults / minors

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this means the ברייתא now says slaves and בני שפחות are the same in every way. The comparison is only about the adult/minor rule. For slaves bought from גוים, immersion alone is still not enough to stop them from making wine forbidden. The ruling that immersed slaves do not forbid wine still applies only to בני שפחות.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
slaves are similar to sons of maidservants.
Just as with sons of maidservants,
it is the adults who make wine into libation wine,
but minors do not make wine into libation wine,
so too with slaves:
adults make wine into libation wine,
but minors do not make wine into libation wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by finding a new purpose for "וכן" that works for every opinion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of what the linking word "וכן" teaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "וכן" seemed to have no purpose for the opinion that spittle and treading are pure.
steps.terutzMaskana: "וכן" teaches that slaves follow the same adult/minor rule as בני שפחות for יין נסך.

steps.title: This rejects רב's view about a one-day-old baby
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this lesson comes to reject רב, who held that even a one-day-old gentile baby makes wine into יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: This comes to exclude the view of רב. רב said that even a one-day-old baby makes wine into יין נסך. The ברייתא teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows who disagrees with the lesson it just found. The ברייתא's rule that minors do not make wine forbidden goes against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב held that any gentile, even a newborn, makes wine forbidden by touching it. The ברייתא, as just explained, says only adults do. So the ברייתא argues with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to reject a different view
A one-day-old baby
That it is not so

steps.whatToRemember: Under this reading of the ברייתא, only adult slaves and adult בני שפחות make wine into יין נסך. This goes against רב, who said even a one-day-old baby does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how far the rule of touch-forbidden wine reaches. It tells us whether a young child's touch makes wine forbidden.

phrases.english: This is to exclude the view of רב,
as רב said:

phrases.aramaic: תִּינוֹק בֶּן יוֹמוֹ עוֹשֶׂה יֵין נֶסֶךְ,
phrases.english: A one-day-old baby makes wine into libation wine.
phrases.notes: He means a gentile baby who touches the wine.

phrases.english: It teaches us that this is not so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the opposing view that the lesson of step 7 rejects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minors do not make wine into יין נסך, against רב, who holds that even a one-day-old baby does.

steps.title: A gentile stirs wine in a Jewish store in מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: A גוי asks for wine, is told there is none, and stirs his hand in a bucket of wine. The angry storeowner then dumps that wine into a whole barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident in מחוזא. A גוי came into a Jew's store and asked, "Do you have wine to sell?" They said, "No." Wine was sitting in a bucket. He put his hand into it, stirred it around, and said, "Isn't this wine?" The storeowner grabbed the bucket and, in his anger, threw it into a barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a real-life story. This step only sets up the case; the ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי's touch and stirring made the bucket's wine a problem. Then the owner poured that wine into a full barrel. So the question becomes what happens to the whole barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident, a real case
Wine
A bucket
Stirred, swished around
Anger
A barrel

phrases.english: There was a certain incident in מחוזא:
a גוי came and entered a Jew's store.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִית לְכוּ חַמְרָא לְזַבּוֹנֵי?
phrases.english: He said to them: Do you have wine to sell?
They said to him: No.
There was wine sitting in a bucket.
He put his hand into it and stirred it around.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: הַאי לָאו חַמְרָא הוּא?
phrases.english: He said to them: Isn't this wine?
The other one took it, in his anger,
phrases.notes: "The other one" is the Jewish storeowner.

phrases.english: and threw it into a barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a real case of a גוי touching and stirring wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Case setup: wine stirred by a גוי was mixed into a whole barrel of wine.

steps.title: רבא permits selling the barrel to gentiles; others forbid it
steps.stepSummary: רבא allowed the barrel to be sold to גוים. רב הונא בר חיננא and רב הונא בריה דרב נחמן disagreed, and both sides announced their rulings publicly with שופר blasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא allowed the wine to be sold to גוים. רב הונא בר חיננא and רב הונא, son of רב נחמן, disagreed with him. שופר blasts went out from רבא's court permitting it, and שופר blasts went out from the court of רב הונא בר חיננא and רב הונא בר רב נחמן forbidding it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the rulings on the barrel from the story. The rabbis disagree, and each side publicly announces its ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא held that the wine may at least be used for benefit, so it can be sold to גוים. The two רב הונאs held that even benefit is forbidden, so it may not be sold. The שופר blasts show this was a public, strongly held disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: He permitted it
To sell to gentiles
Disagreed with him
Shofar blasts (used to announce a ruling publicly)
They forbade

steps.confusionAlert: רבא did not allow a Jew to drink this wine. He only allowed selling it to גוים, which means getting benefit from it.

phrases.english: רבא permitted it to be sold to גוים.
Disagreeing with him were

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב הוּנָא בַּר רַב נַחְמָן וְאָסְרִי.
phrases.english: and רב הונא בר רב נחמן and forbade it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rulings on the case described in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא allows selling the barrel to גוים, meaning benefit is permitted. רב הונא בר חיננא and רב הונא בר רב נחמן forbid it.
